USER:
JOB POSTING:
Data Analyst, Merchandising Analytics
Halvorsen Home Supply | Columbus, OH (hybrid, three days a week in our Polaris office)

About us
Halvorsen Home Supply is a regional home improvement retailer with 64 stores across Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky and western Pennsylvania, plus a growing online business. Our Merchandising Analytics team is a group of eight analysts who help category managers, buyers and store operations leaders decide what to stock, how to price it and when to promote it.

The role
We are hiring a Data Analyst to own weekly sales, margin and inventory reporting for two of our largest departments, building materials and seasonal. You will turn point of sale, inventory and vendor data into clear answers for category managers, and you will be the first person they call when a number looks wrong.

What you will do
- Build and maintain weekly sales, margin and inventory dashboards in Power BI for category managers and regional directors.
- Write SQL against our Snowflake data warehouse to answer ad hoc questions about product, store and promotion performance.
- Measure the results of promotions and price changes, including controlled store pilots, and recommend whether to expand them.
- Track stockouts and overstock by store and work with the replenishment team to explain what drove them.
- Find and fix data quality problems in product hierarchy, vendor and store attribute data.
- Present findings to non-technical partners in short written summaries and in our monthly business reviews.

What we are looking for
- Three or more years of experience in a data analyst, reporting analyst or similar role.
- Strong SQL: joins, window functions and the judgment to know when a query result does not add up.
- Advanced Excel and hands-on experience with a BI tool (Power BI preferred, Tableau or Looker welcome).
- A bachelor's degree in statistics, economics, mathematics, computer science or a related quantitative field.
- Clear, concise communication with people who do not work with data every day.

Nice to have
- Python or R for analysis and automation.
- Experience with retail, distribution or supply chain data.
- Familiarity with Snowflake or another cloud data warehouse.

What we offer
- Salary range of $72,000 to $88,000, plus an annual bonus.
- Medical, dental and vision coverage, a 401(k) with a 5 percent match and an employee discount.
- Fifteen days of paid time off in your first year, plus paid holidays.

APPLICATION A:
Tamika Jackson
Columbus, OH | (614) 555-0116 | tamika.jackson@gmail.com

SUMMARY
Retail operations analyst with more than a decade in large format stores, including six years running a store with a $14 million annual sales plan. Moved onto the company's operations analytics team in 2025 and now owns store performance reporting, writes basic SQL for inventory, sales and labor questions, and works with allocation on stock problems. Knows how product, staffing and promotions actually play out on a sales floor, and uses that context to catch numbers that do not match reality.

EXPERIENCE
Operations Analyst | Summit Ridge Outfitters, Columbus, OH | May 2025 to Present
• Produce weekly store scorecards for 52 locations covering sales to plan, conversion, units per transaction, labor hours and shrink; built in Excel, with a Power BI version now in pilot with two district managers.
• Write SQL against the company's SQL Server warehouse for ad hoc requests from merchandising and store operations, mostly joins and aggregations, often adapting saved queries from senior analysts on the team.
• Investigated an overstock problem in seasonal outerwear and showed that allocation still used prior year sales at stores that had since lost floor space. The allocation team reviewed the finding for next season.
• Built a weekly out of stock report that flags top selling footwear and camping items with zero on hand at any store, which the replenishment team uses to prioritize transfers.
• Built a markdown tracking workbook that matches clearance price changes to sell-through by store, used in the post season review.
• Act as the link between the analytics team and store managers, turning field requests into clear report requirements.

Store Manager | Summit Ridge Outfitters, Columbus, OH | Apr 2019 to Apr 2025
• Ran a 38,000 square foot store with about $14 million in annual sales and a team of 45 full and part time employees.
• Beat the sales plan by 9% in 2023 after reworking the front of store seasonal layout based on item level sales and margin reports.
• Cut shrink from 2.1% to 1.3% of sales over two years through cycle count discipline, receiving audits and loss reviews with district asset protection.
• Built an Excel tool for weekly labor scheduling against forecasted traffic, later adopted by four nearby stores.
• Managed replenishment exceptions and vendor direct deliveries for the camping, footwear and outerwear departments.
• Hired and trained five department leads, two of whom went on to run stores.

Assistant Store Manager | Summit Ridge Outfitters, Columbus, OH | Jul 2015 to Mar 2019
• Led receiving, stocking and price change execution for a store carrying 30,000 SKUs.
• Prepared the weekly sales recap and payroll reports for the store manager and district office.
• Coordinated two full store remodels, keeping the store open and on schedule.

EDUCATION
Bachelor of Science in Statistics, The Ohio State University, 2015

SKILLS
Data and reporting: SQL (SQL Server, joins, aggregations), Excel (pivot tables, XLOOKUP, Power Query), Power BI (report building, learning DAX)
Retail operations: store P&L, labor scheduling, inventory replenishment, shrink control, markdown management, planogram execution
Systems: Oracle Retail, Blue Yonder workforce management, Microsoft 365

ADDITIONAL
• Completed an online SQL for data analysis course (2024) and the Microsoft Learn Power BI data analyst learning path (2025)
• Volunteer at a Columbus nonprofit bike shop, tracking donated bikes and repair parts in a shared spreadsheet
